findings.plan_section: Section 5 (Ba kênh và unique-case budget) & Section 11 Q1
findings.title: RRF per-channel unique-case cap (100), channel pool retention (100 vs 20), and coverage/exhaustion denominator rules need explicit specification
findings.evidence_and_counterexample: 1) Existing helper `fuse_case_ranks(channels, limit=20, k=60)` in `pipeline_v2/retrieval/bm25.py` calls `rank_cases(hits)` with `limit=None`. Counterexample `CE05_rrf_channel_cap_bug` in `test_plan_counterexamples.py` proves that if one channel scans 2,048 raw hits (yielding >100 unique cases) while another yields 100, un-capped ranks >100 (e.g. rank 150 contributing `1/(60+150)`) cause a rank inversion at top-1 between `CASE_X.txt` and `CASE_Y.txt`. Conversely, `optimization_v2/index.py` line 211 (`rank_cases(hits, limit)`) truncated per-channel output to the final output `limit=20` instead of `channel_case_budget=100`, dropping ranks 21..100 needed by `SOURCE_CHUNK_INDEX.md` Section 5 ('Giữ union trước cap và pool sau cap'). 2) Counterexample `CE02` & `CE03`: When `query_case` is in the 7,708-case train universe, maximum eligible cases is `N - 1 = 7,707` (not `7,708`). In Dense search (`415,693` points), cosine similarity is defined for all eligible passages (`>= 414,553` points), so at `scan_cap=4096` Dense is NEVER `universe_exhausted`; if `unique_cases < 100` at 4096, it must report `capped=True, universe_exhausted=False, budget_shortfall=True`. In Lexical BM25 (`score > 0`), checking `len(returned) < scan_limit` fails when total positive hits equals `scan_limit` (e.g. 256); `total_positive_hits` from `len(scores)` must determine `universe_exhausted`.
findings.impact: Without explicit pre-fusion truncation to `channel_case_budget=100` per channel, channels with fewer duplicates get extra RRF votes beyond rank 100. Truncating channel diagnostics to 20 instead of 100 loses pre-cap recall visibility. Using `7,708` instead of `7,707` when `query_case` is excluded makes `universe_exhausted` impossible to reach.
findings.recommended_change: Specify in Section 5 & Section 7: (a) Each channel deduplicates raw hits by best-hit rank and truncates to `channel_case_budget=100` unique cases BEFORE feeding `fuse_case_ranks`; (b) Response preserves both the 100-case per-channel ranked list (or union summary) and the 20-case post-RRF finalist list, with `max_leads_per_case` (e.g., 3) bounded per returned candidate; (c) Define `eligible_case_universe = 7707` when `query_case` is in train (`7708` only in out-of-corpus diagnostic mode) and distinguish `universe_exhausted` (all positive BM25 hits or all eligible points scanned) from `scan_capped` (`raw_scanned == scan_cap` with unseen eligible points remaining) and `budget_shortfall` (`returned_unique_cases < channel_case_budget`).
findings.acceptance_test: Unit test with `CE01`, `CE02`, `CE05`: verify that rank 101+ in any channel contributes 0.0 to RRF, that `channel_case_budget=100` is retained in channel metadata while `results` has `limit=20`, and that `eligible_case_universe=7707` and `budget_shortfall=True, universe_exhausted=False` hold when 5 long cases flood 4,096 raw hits.

findings.plan_section: Section 3 (Session và kiểm tra toàn vẹn), Section 5 (Ba kênh) & Section 11 Q2, Q3
findings.title: Qdrant `exact=True` cold timeout (60s internal limit), single-pass vs multi-round `exact=True` scan, and `ReadonlyCache` shard fan-out verification cost
findings.evidence_and_counterexample: Empirical measurement on `coliee_m3_full_ef2f4d6950a5b9fd` (`probe_results.json` & `probe_deep_dive_results.json`): 1) The first cold `exact=True` query failed with HTTP 500 (`Service internal error: Timeout error: Operation 'Search' timed out after 59.999781103s`) because `QdrantStore.search` only sets client HTTP `timeout=120` and omits Qdrant's URL query parameter `?timeout=120`. 2) Once warm, `exact=True` takes `2.42s` at `limit=4096` and `2.65s` at `limit=256`—identical latency because `exact=True` scans all 415,693 vectors regardless of `limit`. Running geometric expansion (`256 -> 512 -> 1024 -> 2048 -> 4096`) as 5 separate Qdrant `exact=True` RPC calls would wastefully scan all 415,693 vectors up to 5 times (`~13s` warm, `>60s` cold). 3) Because `schedule` sorted passages by `full_input_tokens` across 6,496 `.npz` shards, `4,096` raw hits span `2,860` distinct shards (`probe_deep_dive_results.json`). At `10.875ms` per shard load + SHA-256 verification, checking all 4,096 raw hits against `ReadonlyCache` costs `~31s` of disk I/O per query, whereas verifying the retained unique-case leads (`100` unique cases) touches only `97` shards (`~1.0s` cold, `<0.1s` with LRU cache).
findings.impact: Without `?timeout=120` on Qdrant's query endpoint, cold `exact=True` queries fail with HTTP 500. Issuing multiple `exact=True` RPC rounds and verifying all 4,096 raw hits against `.npz` shards inflates single-query dense latency from `~3.5s` to `>45s`.
findings.recommended_change: Specify in Section 3 & Section 5: (a) Pass `?timeout=120` (matching profile `timeout_seconds`) to Qdrant `/points/query`; (b) For `exact=True`, allow either a single Qdrant query at `scan_cap=4096` (or `256 -> 4096` two-step) since Qdrant scans all 415,693 vectors on every `exact=True` call anyway, then perform adaptive windowing `256 -> 512 -> 1024 -> 2048 -> 4096` in memory to stop at the smallest window achieving `100` unique cases; (c) Verify payload and cosine score against `ReadonlyCache` shards (with bounded LRU shard cache and SQLite `schedule` `passage_id -> batch` lookup) for all retained unique-case passage leads (`<= 100 * max_leads_per_case` hits) and boundary hits, rather than loading 2,860 shards for discarded sibling hits.
findings.acceptance_test: Test Qdrant adapter passes `timeout` param; verify that when 1 case floods 1,000 raw hits, `full_search` completes dense retrieval + shard vector attestation within bounded shard reads (`<= unique_cases * max_leads_per_case` shards) and catches any mutated vector or payload among retained hits.

findings.plan_section: Section 5 (Ba kênh) & Section 8 (Telemetry và vận hành)
findings.title: `PersistentBM25.search` on `passage` must not be called repeatedly in geometric expansion and should avoid redundant per-posting `documents` table lookups
findings.evidence_and_counterexample: Empirical measurement (`probe_deep_dive_results.json` & `probe_mmap_and_open_results.json`): `PersistentBM25.search` in `optimization_v2/index.py` already computes `scores[ident]` for ALL matching documents in the corpus (`328,265` passages across `7,707` cases for a 6-term legal query) before sorting and slicing `[:limit]`. On the 4.36 GB `lexical.sqlite3`, a single `passage` query with `JOIN documents` takes `104.2s` cold / `63.6s` warm; preloading the 415,693 `(id, length)` pairs in session memory (`~25 MB`) and filtering `exclude_case` by prefix/map without joining the heavy `documents` metadata table cuts query time in half (`52.2s`) with 100% identical ranking (`bm25_join_vs_nojoin_exact_match=True`). Calling `PersistentBM25.search` 5 times for `256 -> 512 -> 1024 -> 2048 -> 4096` would multiply this cost by 5x for zero benefit.
findings.impact: Re-running SQLite BM25 queries across expansion rounds would take 5–8 minutes per query. Calling `get_many('passage', ids)` on all 4,096 raw hits also deserializes 4,096 JSON rows when only `<= 100 * max_leads_per_case` are needed.
findings.recommended_change: Specify in Section 5: (a) `case_bm25` has 1 row per case (`raw_hits == unique_cases`), so it queries `limit = channel_case_budget` (100) directly with no geometric expansion; (b) `passage_bm25` scores matching postings in a single SQLite pass (using in-memory `(id -> length, case_id)` lookup initialized in the read-only session plus read-only SQLite `PRAGMA mmap_size` / `cache_size`), walks the sorted `(score, passage_id)` list once up to `scan_cap=4096` to select the 100 unique cases and bounded passage leads, and calls `get_many` only on the selected passage IDs.
findings.acceptance_test: Verify `passage_bm25` executes exactly 1 SQLite term-postings pass regardless of whether the 100th unique case falls at raw rank 120 or raw rank 3,500, and returns identical ranks/scores to the reference BM25 oracle.

findings.plan_section: Section 5 (Tie-break & Dense boundary ties) & Section 11 Q1, Q3
findings.title: Real corpus contains thousands of bit-identical passages across different cases causing massive exact cosine ties in Qdrant
findings.evidence_and_counterexample: Empirical probe (`probe_results.json` & `CE03`): Short passages (e.g., boilerplate judgement lines, `[Traduction]`, `<FRAGMENT_SUPPRESSED>`) have identical text and therefore identical vectors across up to `1,898` distinct cases (`2,459` tied points with cosine `1.0` in top-4096). Because Qdrant breaks exact score ties by internal point UUID (`uuid5(NAMESPACE, fp + ':' + passage_id)`), not by `(passage_id, case_id)`, any cut across a tie group at `scan_cap` or at the 100th unique case depends on UUID order.
findings.impact: If the local verifier or ranker re-sorts tied hits by `(passage_id, case_id)` without recognizing that Qdrant's `limit` cut across a tie group by UUID, a test might falsely claim deterministic corpus-wide tie resolution when unseen tied points exist at rank `limit + 1`.
findings.recommended_change: Keep Section 5's honest rule ('không hứa ID set ổn định tuyệt đối khi server cắt qua tie; trả `boundary_tie/coverage_uncertainty`') and make the implementation rule explicit: (a) Within the fetched raw hits, normalize scores within `tie_atol` (or exact float32 equality) or preserve Qdrant order while recording `boundary_tie_detected = (abs(last_included_score - next_excluded_score) <= tie_atol)` (or when `len(raw_hits) == scan_cap` and the tail forms a tie run); (b) Never claim a tie group at the `scan_cap` boundary is fully resolved.
findings.acceptance_test: Fixture `CE03` with >100 candidate cases sharing identical vector cosine score: verify `boundary_tie_detected=True` is emitted in channel coverage metadata.

findings.title: Unicode `.casefold()` offset drift and cross-chunk phrase boundaries require explicit raw-byte offset mapping
findings.evidence_and_counterexample: Counterexample `CE08_phrase_casefold_offset` in `test_plan_counterexamples.py`: 1) In M2 (`m2_passages_20261106_v1`), `48,990` headings and all inter-unit whitespace are excluded from passages (`excluded_structural_views`), and adjacent paragraphs are never merged (`merge_parents=False`). Any phrase crossing a heading-to-paragraph boundary or paragraph-to-paragraph boundary has 0% recall in passage-only search. 2) In Unicode, characters like `'ß'` (`'Straßenbahn'`), `'İ'`, or ligatures expand under `.casefold()` (1 codepoint -> 2+ codepoints). Computing `text.casefold().find(needle.casefold())` and feeding that offset into `Utf8Map.char_to_byte()` shifts the returned byte span (`'décision est raisonnable'` becomes `'décision est raisonnabl'`), failing raw hash/slice verification.
findings.impact: Naive case-insensitive substring search corrupts raw `span_bytes` whenever a multi-char casefold character precedes the match in the same document.
findings.recommended_change: Specify in Section 6: (a) `search_phrase` scans raw case streams (via `RawReader` / `Utf8Map`), covering all 7,708 cases including headings, whitespace, and unnumbered regions; (b) Support two explicit baseline modes: `exact_case_sensitive` (direct UTF-8 byte or codepoint match) and `unicode_casefold_mapped` using an explicit per-character index map `fold_char_idx -> orig_char_idx -> Utf8Map.char_to_byte(orig_char_idx)` (as demonstrated in `CE08`), plus verify `raw[a:b].decode('utf-8').casefold() == needle.casefold()` before returning every span; (c) Reject any BM25 pre-filter for phrase search unless all `analyze(needle)` tokens are proven non-empty and substring-safe under the active matching mode.
findings.acceptance_test: Test `CE08` with French/German/ligature characters (`ß`, `İ`, `é`, `ﬁ`), CRLF, and UTF-8 BOM (`\ufeff`) before a cross-paragraph and cross-heading phrase match; assert `raw[a:b]` decodes cleanly and its `casefold()` equals `needle.casefold()`.

findings.plan_section: Section 7 (Response và evidence delivery) & Section 11 Q5
findings.title: `open_source` 64 KiB pagination requires interval-set cursor state, UTF-8 codepoint boundary snapping, fast sealed M2 loading, and full M1/M2 role metadata on components
findings.evidence_and_counterexample: Empirical findings (`probe_mmap_and_open_results.json` & `CE10`): 1) Across the 7,708 train cases, `5` single parent units and `13` expanded `prev + parent + next` windows exceed `64 KiB` (`65,536` bytes), up to `85,392` bytes in `041666.txt` (`p000416`/`p000417`). When a hit (`12b`) lies in the middle of an `84,205`-byte parent (`041666.txt` `p000417`) and Page 1 delivers the hit-centered window, the remaining undelivered portions of `parent` form TWO disjoint byte intervals (`[parent_start, window_start]` and `[window_end, parent_end]`) plus `previous_context` and `next_context`. A simple scalar cursor offset loses the leading prefix of `parent`. 2) Slicing raw bytes at `byte_budget` inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character (`é`, `“`, `—`) raises `UnicodeDecodeError` unless snapped down via `Utf8Map`. 3) `PassageReader.open_context` currently calls `PassageReader._case()`, which re-runs M1 `parse_source`, M2 `build_case_navigation`, and Qwen3 `build_case_passages` on the entire case (`2.46s` for `055641.txt` per call!). 4) `NavigationReader.open_context` currently returns `components` with only `{kind, handle, unit_id, span_bytes}`, omitting `paragraph_role` (`quoted`/`unknown`), `observed_marker`, `uncertainties`, `role_evidence_refs`, and any intervening `unnumbered` unit between `previous_paragraph` and `parent`.
findings.impact: Scalar cursor pagination drops parent prefixes on middle hits (`041666.txt`); un-snapped byte caps crash on multi-byte UTF-8; calling `PassageReader._case()` in hot search/open paths adds seconds of redundant re-tokenization; omitting `paragraph_role`/`uncertainties` hides `quoted/unknown` status from M4.
findings.recommended_change: Specify in Section 7: (a) Snap all byte-budget cuts to valid UTF-8 codepoint boundaries via `Utf8Map`; (b) Represent cursor/delivery state as ordered byte-interval lists (`requested_spans`, `delivered_spans`, `pending_spans` per component `parent`, `previous_context`, `next_context`) so middle-of-parent hits never lose the parent prefix; (c) Allow caller-configurable `byte_budget` (`1 <= byte_budget <= 65536`, default `65536`) and explicitly mark `token_safe_agent_payload=False`; (d) Enrich each returned component with `unit_kind`, `observed_marker`, `paragraph_role`, `uncertainties`, `role_evidence_refs`, `language_region`, and explicitly list any intervening `unnumbered` units between `previous_ref`/`parent_ref`/`next_ref`; (e) In a validated session where M2 bundle `seal.json` is verified, read per-case M2 JSON directly by verifying its `seal.json` SHA-256 and raw `source_hash` (`<2ms`) instead of re-running Qwen3 tokenization on every open/preview.
findings.acceptance_test: Test `open_source` on real case `041666.txt` (`p000416`/`p000417`, `85,392` bytes) and `055641.txt` (`u000001`/`p000351`), plus synthetic middle-hit and multi-byte UTF-8 boundary fixtures: verify union of `delivered_spans` across pages equals exact `requested_spans` with zero gap/overlap, `<50ms` per open, and full preservation of `quoted`/`unknown` role metadata.

findings.plan_section: Section 2, Section 3, Section 4 & Section 11 Q2, Q6
findings.title: Read-only isolation of sealed `m3_full_train_20261108_v1` and query-reading / navigation map helper alignment
findings.evidence_and_counterexample: 1) `m3_full_train_20261108_v1` contains sealed ingestion artifacts (`manifest.json`, `lexical.sqlite3`, `seal.json`, `ledger.sqlite3`, `execution_state.json`, `run_result.json`). In `optimization_v2/runtime.py`, query embedding wrote to `<index_dir>_runtime/ledger.sqlite3` and `compatibility_current.json`. If `full_search` writes query embedding attempts or search logs into `m3_full_train_20261108_v1/ledger.sqlite3` or mutates `execution_state.json`, it will alter the accepted ingestion ledger (`3812f4d1...`). 2) Section 4 defines `search_case(query_case)` and `open_source`, while `SOURCE_CHUNK_INDEX.md` Section 3.5 also specifies paginated navigation map (`map(case_id, offset, limit)`) and `anchors`/`source_anchors` inspection so the agent can read a long query case before formulating search queries.
findings.impact: Writing query attempts into the ingestion `ledger.sqlite3` would break immutability of the accepted M3 full ingestion run. Omitting a thin `get_case_map` / `inspect_case` exposure in the session API would force M4 to open raw M2 readers separately.
findings.recommended_change: 1) Enforce that `m3_full_train_20261108_v1` is strictly read-only (`?mode=ro` on both `lexical.sqlite3` and `ledger.sqlite3`); all search session ledgers, query embedding receipts, and request logs must be written to a dedicated search runtime directory (e.g., `pipeline_v2/artifacts/m3_search_runtime_...` or caller-specified log dir). 2) Expose thin read-only delegation methods on the search session (`case_map`, `case_anchors`, `open_query` / `open_source`) backed by the already-verified M2 navigation bundle so query-reading and candidate-reading share one provenance guard.
findings.acceptance_test: Verify SHA-256 of all files in `pipeline_v2/artifacts/m3_full_train_20261108_v1/` (including `ledger.sqlite3` and `execution_state.json`) is 100% unchanged before and after running `search_corpus`, `search_case`, `search_phrase`, `search_identity`, and `open_source`.
